chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Politeness with the people is half the Emān, and kindness with them is half the life'.

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Mingle with the righteous secretly and mingle with the immoral superficially (in public), but do not be attracted to them as they would oppress you. There will come a time, when, from the religious people, only those will be safe who are thought of as fools, and they would patience so much so that they will be called silly i.e. there is no intellect for him'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'modaraya' (politeness/adaptability) in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of *al-mudarāh* (social tact) as half of faith, linking interpersonal kindness directly to spiritual sustenance. It advises a strategic duality: maintaining sincere, private piety with the righteous while engaging openly with the wicked to avoid being overwhelmed, a practice rooted in the principle of *Taqiyyah* (prudence) during times of social pressure. The warning against being perceived as 'foolish' underscores the practical wisdom required to preserve religious identity in hostile environments.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Politeness with the people is half the Emān, and kindness with them is half the life’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Mingle with the righteous secretly and mingle with the immoral superficially (in public), but do not be attracted to them as they would oppress you. There will come a time, when, from the religious people, only those will be safe who are thought of as fools, and they would patience so much so that they will be called silly i.e. there is no intellect for him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqa from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Dealing kindly with people is half of belief and leniency to them is half of livelihood.’

The Imam then said, ‘Meet the virtuous people privately. Meet the criminals in public and do not be attracted to them; they will do injustice to you. There will come a time when, from the religious people, only those will be safe who are thought of as fools. They exercise patience so much so that they will be called silly.’”
